reader_notes: Register is markedly literary for ELF — long periodic sentences ('A cumulative list is a ratchet', 'or it is a shoal with a name') reward a second read but never collapse on one; a strong student will be slowed rather than blocked.

Q3 A requires the arithmetic 19/61 to be recognised as just under a third; the passage supplies both numbers plainly ('sixty-one plant species', 'nineteen were found in each of the last three surveys'), so the step is fair, but it is the only question in the unit with a computational move.

Q4 A is the strongest trap: it is directionally close to the Odren facts but overstates them (the plants 'thinned by half', they did not die), so the discrimination rests on precision rather than on comprehension of the point.
